newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise on Yeltsin return, Brady rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise on Yeltsin return, Brady rise.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose on Wednesday, tracking U.S. Treasuries and other Brady bonds, and dealers said President Boris Yeltsin's arrival in the Kremlin boosted demand as well.
Yeltsin, who left hospital only on Monday after treatment for pneumonia, went to the Kremlin on Wednesday for talks with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
"MinFins followed U.S. Treasuries and Bradies' rise, while Yeltsin's news was the other encouraging factor," Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said.
Dealers said demand was mainly from Western banks, while some Russian banks were selling. The fourth and fifth tranches were traded the most actively.
"Yields seem still attractive for Western investors. London is buying actively," an ICFI Moscow Partners dealer said.
